question: List the core Stellar operation types available in a classic transaction — enumerate the main operations and what each does.

golden.answer: A transaction is the signed, atomic unit that bundles one or more operations. Classic operation types: CreateAccount, Payment, PathPaymentStrictSend/Receive; ManageBuyOffer, ManageSellOffer, CreatePassiveSellOffer; ChangeTrust, SetTrustLineFlags; SetOptions, AccountMerge, ManageData, BumpSequence; claimable-balance, liquidity-pool, clawback and sponsorship operations; and Soroban InvokeHostFunction, ExtendFootprintTTL, RestoreFootprint. There are no ERC-style Transfer, Mint or Burn operations.
keyFacts: A transaction bundles one or more operations atomically and is the signed unit.
Names the main payment, offer, trustline, account and Soroban operations.
There are no Transfer, Mint or Burn operations.
avoid: Do NOT invent operation names or say operations are signed and submitted on their own.
golden.notes: Legacy AllowTrust and Inflation need not be listed.

sources.note: OperationType enum byte-identical to v27.0; no TRANSFER/MINT/BURN.

corroboration.claim: Per the official complete operation list as of 2026-08-29, classic Stellar has no ERC-style Transfer, Mint, or Burn operations.

evidence.note: Exact page heading: ‘List of Operations’. Exact description: ‘Explore the full list of Stellar operations’; that list contains no ERC-style `Transfer`, `Mint`, or `Burn` classic operation.

The exhaustive primary list contains no classic operations with those ERC-style names, and no primary result contradicted that absence.
